summary: Throttle ladder gap causing interleaved upload rejections for mixed realtime and bulk traffic
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports sudden waves of 429s on a dedicated pool during a mixed workload: many short-lived realtime chat requests interleaved with periodic bulk file uploads. Throttles appear to escalate rapidly and do not smooth out within expected refill windows.

Impact:
- Intermittent user-facing errors in chat frontend for ~12k active sessions (10-15% error rate during spike).
- Several bulk ingest jobs aborted mid-upload, causing downstream reconciliation failures in Neptune Analytics pipeline.
- Customer requests urgent guidance and possible emergency config change to avoid data loss.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool: dp-us-east-7 (customer-owned dedicated lease)
- Region: us-east-1
- API endpoint: https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate and /v1/uploads
- Auth: signed URL + ephemeral API keys for workers

Steps to reproduce (as provided by customer):
1) Start a steady stream of short chat requests at ~400 rps (payload ~150 tokens).
2) Trigger concurrent bulk uploads: 6 parallel multipart uploads, each with 50 parts, triggered every 90s by their orchestrator.
3) Observe that within ~3 minutes of the orchestrator start, chat sessions receive 429s and multipart uploads begin failing with 429 on part uploads.
4) Customer notes that regenerating signed URLs for a subset of workers temporarily reduces errors for ~30s then 429s return.

Customer-provided logs (excerpt):
[2026-03-10T09:14:12Z] worker-17 POST /v1/uploads/part 429 {"code":"rate_exceeded","window_ms":60000,"remaining":0} 
[2026-03-10T09:14:13Z] chat-frontend POST /v1/generate 429 {"code":"rate_exceeded","bucket":"priority-lane","refill_interval_ms":1000} 
[2026-03-10T09:14:45Z] orchestrator INFO Multipart abort: 3/50 failed parts due to 429

Notes from customer: signed-url renewal correlates with short-lived improvement; they suspect some agents are double-counting tokens when switching to new ephemeral keys.
investigation_notes:
Initial hypothesis:
- Rate-limiter ladder (priority lanes + background bulk pool) is misaligning refill windows across edge proxies and origin token accounting when signed URLs are rotated rapidly.
- Health checks / heartbeat traffic from the orchestrator may be consuming burst credits in the background pool, causing priority-lane consumer requests to be more aggressively rejected by the shared tenant budget.

Actions taken so far:
- Reproduced high-level pattern in staging by running mixed chat + multipart jobs against a dedicated-reservation replica (test-dp-3). Confirmed 429 waves after mixing short-live streams with multipart part uploads.
- Collected token accounting traces from rate-limiter service between edge-proxy and origin for dp-us-east-7: saw refill drift of ~400ms between nodes during high ingress, causing ephemeral keys to appear to consume separate buckets briefly.
- Correlated with proxy logs showing many small TCP connect/close cycles from orchestrator workers (keepalive disabled) which incremented per-connection counters.

Open questions:
- Are the signed-url renewals creating ephemeral-key churn that triggers per-key bucket initialization (double-count) on the edge?
- Is the burst/bulk pool meant to be fully isolated from priority-lane accounting on Dedicated leases, or are they intentionally shared by default?

comments: 2026-03-10T12:05: Carlos Ortega: Acknowledged and started investigation. Requested customer to share ingestion schedule and exact signed-url rotation timing.
2026-03-10T13:18: Maya Chen: Customer uploaded orchestrator schedule and confirmed signed-url rotation every 45s for worker pool; keepalive disabled on their uploader so connections are short-lived.
2026-03-10T15:02: SRE (Priya Patel): Reproduced in staging; see rate-limiter trace. We'll run an experiment disabling per-connection counting on edge-7 for this tenant.

2026-03-11T09:30: Carlos Ortega: Ran config patch (disable per-connection counters for dp-us-east-7) in canary; initial canary reduced 429s for chat but bulk uploads still retried and occasionally failed.
2026-03-11T11:45: Maya Chen: Customer confirmed decreased chat errors but wants durable fix for multipart uploads; asking whether priority/bulk pools can be split for dedicated lease.

2026-03-12T08:00: Carlos Ortega: Filing follow-up with Product (linked PR) to clarify default pool isolation for Dedicated. Proposed immediate mitigation: request to enable separate burst pool for Neptune Analytics while we roll a config change.
resolution:
WORKAROUND applied: Enabled isolated burst pool for tenant neptune (dp-us-east-7) on edge-7 and disabled per-connection counting. Immediate effect: chat 429s dropped from ~12% to <1% during the same workload; multipart uploads reduced aborted parts by ~80%.

Root cause (tentative): Combination of ephemeral-key churn from signed-url rotation + short TCP connections caused per-node bucket initializations and inconsistent accounting across proxies. That plus shared burst credits between priority-lane and background bulk pool produced fast throttle escalation when orchestrator heartbeat and multipart part uploads interleaved with realtime chat.

Permanent fix / follow-ups:
- Product to review default rate-limiter ladder behavior for Dedicated leases: PR #489 pending to add opt-in strict pool isolation per-tenant. (Assigned to rate-limiter team)
- Engineering: Add de-duplication for ephemeral-key bucket initialization across edges to avoid transient double-counting on key rotation. (Linked PR above)
- Documentation: Add best-practice note for customers using signed-url rotation + short-lived connections: recommend enabling keepalive, staggered rotation, or dedicated burst pool configuration. (CS / Docs)
- Postmortem: If customer impact persists after full rollout, open incident with follow-up timeline.
next_steps:
1) Product to review and merge PR for tenant burst-pool isolation.
2) Engineering to schedule de-duplication change in next sprint and provide ETA.
3) CS to share mitigation checklist with customer: enable keepalive on uploader, stagger signed-url rotations, or request isolated burst pool.
4) Monitor dp-us-east-7 telemetry for 48 hours post-change; customer to report any residual errors.
customer_communication_summary: Customer informed of temporary mitigation (isolated burst pool + per-connection counting disabled). Provided guidance to change keepalive and rotation cadence. Customer requested ETA for permanent fix; Product/Eng engaged.
